questions.stem: A cylinder has a volume of $200\pi\text{ cm}^3$ and a radius of $5\text{ cm}$. What is its height?
questions.explanation: $V = \pi r^2 h$, so $200\pi = \pi \times 25 \times h$. Dividing by $25\pi$: $h = 8\text{ cm}$.

questions.stem: A cylindrical water tank has diameter $1.2\text{ m}$ and height $2\text{ m}$. What is its volume in terms of $\pi$?
questions.explanation: Radius $= 0.6\text{ m}$. Volume $= \pi r^2 h = \pi \times 0.36 \times 2 = 0.72\pi\text{ m}^3$.

questions.stem: Two cylinders have the same height. Cylinder A has radius $r$ and Cylinder B has radius $2r$. How many times larger is the volume of Cylinder B compared to Cylinder A?
questions.explanation: Volume of A $= \pi r^2 h$. Volume of B $= \pi (2r)^2 h = 4\pi r^2 h$. So B is $4$ times larger.
